no_lists_because: The item names no list in its own words, input or steps, so it has no example rows to ship.
instructions: 1. Make sure record:business-setup:facts exists and that Stripe and email sending (Resend) are connected; make list:business-setup-checklist and list:business-setup-gaps from the example rows (see pour) if you keep none.

2. Say "Run workflow:recover-failed-payments-and-win-back". The AI starts it with tool:start-a-recipe-run and works the steps in order: read-facts, list-failed-payments, send-the-payment-failed-email, record-the-retry-setting-gap, list-churned-for-win-back, send-the-win-back-email, record-the-stage.
3. Give your own words for the payment-failed email and the win-back (one offer you already sell); the AI checks them with tool:check-copy before it sends.
4. Read the counts: sent and skipped_same_invoice for failed payments (the invoice id is the idempotency key, so a rerun never emails an invoice twice) and sent for win-backs.
5. Set the retry schedule in your Stripe dashboard yourself: no Trillion tool sets it, so the workflow records it as a gap on list:business-setup-gaps.

worked_examples.title: Two failed payments in the last 7 days
worked_examples.ask: Which payments failed this week, and email those buyers.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (step list-failed-payments): the step calls stripe-events-read_money_since with {"since": <unix seconds 7 days ago>} and keeps only failed-payment events, each with customer email, invoice id and amount.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
